variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An advanced search system turns an imperfect query into a small, ordered set of useful results. It combines exact term matching, semantic similarity, hard filters, learned ranking, and product policy because no single signal handles every query well.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate evidence from decisions”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Lexical retrieval
pairs.detail: An inverted index is strong for names, identifiers, quoted phrases, rare terms, and field-aware matching.
pairs.explanation: An inverted index is strong for names, identifiers, quoted phrases, rare terms, and field-aware matching. BM25 is a common scoring function, but the durable idea is term-based evidence.

pairs.label: Semantic retrieval
pairs.detail: An embedding model maps queries and documents into vectors.
pairs.explanation: An embedding model maps queries and documents into vectors. Approximate nearest-neighbor search trades some recall for lower latency and memory than an exact scan.

pairs.label: Structured constraints
pairs.detail: Permissions, tenant, geography, availability, and safety policy are not soft relevance features.
pairs.explanation: Permissions, tenant, geography, availability, and safety policy are not soft relevance features. Enforce them as fail-closed filters at every path that can return a document.

pairs.label: Ranking and policy
pairs.explanation: Fusion combines retrieval evidence. A reranker adds richer query-document features, while diversity and product rules shape the final page without silently overriding safety constraints.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Use the full lesson’s worked examples and interactive labs to explore the trade-offs behind these questions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Lexical retrieval: An inverted index is strong for names, identifiers, quoted phrases, rare terms, and field-aware matching. Semantic retrieval: An embedding model maps queries and documents into vectors. Structured constraints: Permissions, tenant, geography, availability, and safety policy are not soft relevance features. Ranking and policy: Fusion combines retrieval evidence.

pairs.label: Retrieval set
pairs.detail: Measure recall at the exact candidate depth sent to fusion and reranking.
pairs.explanation: Measure recall at the exact candidate depth sent to fusion and reranking. Slice by head and tail queries, locale, filters, new content, and zero-result history.

pairs.label: Ranking set
pairs.detail: Use graded judgments for metrics such as NDCG and inspect pairwise errors.
pairs.explanation: Use graded judgments for metrics such as NDCG and inspect pairwise errors. Keep judgment policy and assessor agreement versioned with the dataset.

pairs.label: Online outcomes
pairs.detail: Measure reformulation, successful click or conversion, abandonment, long click, and task completion where they represent the product goal.
pairs.explanation: Measure reformulation, successful click or conversion, abandonment, long click, and task completion where they represent the product goal.

pairs.label: Operational guardrails
pairs.detail: Reject regressions in tail latency, timeout rate, zero-result rate, freshness, authorization, deletion handling, or infrastructure cost beyond explicit limits.
pairs.explanation: Reject regressions in tail latency, timeout rate, zero-result rate, freshness, authorization, deletion handling, or infrastructure cost beyond explicit limits.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Diagnose symptoms at the owning stage”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Relevant item never appears
pairs.detail: Inspect recall by retriever, filter selectivity, tokenization, embedding versions, ANN parameters, and candidate depth.
pairs.explanation: Inspect recall by retriever, filter selectivity, tokenization, embedding versions, ANN parameters, and candidate depth. Reranker tuning cannot repair a missing candidate.

pairs.label: Good candidates are ordered badly
pairs.detail: Replay source ranks and feature values, check model and feature versions, then compare the fused fallback with the learned order on the affected slice.
pairs.explanation: Replay source ranks and feature values, check model and feature versions, then compare the fused fallback with the learned order on the affected slice.

pairs.label: Only tail latency regresses
pairs.detail: Break down child deadlines, queue time, shard fan-out, cold segments, feature calls, reranker batches, and fallback rate instead of relying on average latency.
pairs.explanation: Break down child deadlines, queue time, shard fan-out, cold segments, feature calls, reranker batches, and fallback rate instead of relying on average latency.

pairs.label: Fast results are stale or forbidden
pairs.detail: Inspect source, representation, and serving lag plus generation skew.
pairs.explanation: Inspect source, representation, and serving lag plus generation skew. Stop serving results whose authorization or deletion state cannot be established.

variants.prompt: Why is reciprocal rank fusion a safer baseline than adding raw lexical and vector scores?
options: It removes the need for candidate limits
It combines rank positions without assuming both engines share a score scale
variants.explanation: RRF uses source ranks, so incompatible score scales do not need ad hoc calibration. It still depends on retrieval coverage and policy enforcement.
